Messages.Author: Ohlmann
Messages.Body:
Why non scarce ? It's one of the only thing that set them apart from other clan.

If you want to play a full Nagaraja crypt, go check how it's done in True Brujah, and don't remove their particularity. Especially since they are extremely scarce in the source.

Edit : in addition, their special are not nagaraja like. Nagaraja are defined by two thing : scarce and with very strange special power. Remove both, and you have orange malkavien.

Messages.Author: Ohlmann
Messages.Body:
If you want to create full nagaraja deck without losing the nagaraja flavor, you'd better see at what set them apart :

* scarce and smallish (well, mid-cap would I say since the four that I have seen played were Le Din Tho, Asguresh, Sennadurek and Anu, which average at 6 cap)

* with strange abilities, most often never seen in other clan.

Even if I have seen Asguresh superstar deck, they use non-nagaraj support for 2/3 of the crypt, because you won't use only one vampire in your crypt  but playing multiple scarce midcap mean they better work very well together.

So, two options :

* the true brujah way : making them a bit fatter, so you can do your deck with only one real vampire. The lack of clan-specific discipline mean they will have to be real powerful and possibly with built-in multiact or something like that.

Example of such a cap 10 :
+ random other discipline ( ?)
Scarce
Can play reaction and block if and only if he is tapped. Untap him after a successful block.
When [this vampire] is acting, reaction card have the additional cost of tapping a ready minion.

* making some support nagaraja that only help nagaraja, but well enough so that paying 3+ additional pool for them can work

Example of such a mid cap :
5 cap

Scarce
When a minion successfully bleed a methuselah for two or more, put a blood from the blood bank on every ready nagaraja you control

This way, playing Anu + him is costly, but his special is awesome (maybe too awesome, it's napkin idea at this level) to help Anu refill.

Messages.Author: Juggernaut1981
Messages.Body:
Direwolf,
Continuing the trend of offering fairly cheap vampires with +MPAs is just like saying 'every discipline needs the tools available to Dominate for the same price or less'. It's dense. +MPAs on a 6cap is a problem. All of the others are 8+ cap.

I can think of a long list of alternative Nagaraja-relevant sorts of abilities that would not require you to give a vampire +MPAs.

1) Gain blood by killing allies.
2) Draw a card by killing a non-mortal ally.
3) Recycle ashheap cards.
4) Built-in Revelations.
5) Built in Compel the Spirit (from any ashheap).
6) Built-in Ex Nihilo (with an option to hunt from Allies).
7) Necromancy Cards cost this vampire 1 less blood.
8) May recruit wraith and zombie allies/retainers as if they met requirements for not extra cost.
9) Burn an ally of yours to gain +hand size for a turn or permanently.

...

Messages.Author: Ohlmann
Messages.Body:
Yes, tapping a vampire is a significant enough cost for MMPA on a 6 cap. Isanwayen is rarely used for MMPA duty, even if a recent win show he can. Most often, it's still a nice option to have but not something you rely on.

Here, you can use your MMPA totem to deflect, block, and even lounge bleed, in addition to MMPA, since govern + conditionning for 5 is more than enough.

In short, she have the same kind of disavantadge in my opinion as Isan (-1 bleed vs harder to rescue), for a more powerful ability, but a less synergistic discipline spread. I would not say the vampire is crazy - she's no prince after all - but still pretty powerful, and certainly more possible source of concern than Isan.
